lessons.title: Fact families
lessons.subject: Math
notes: A fact family uses the same three numbers for related addition and subtraction facts.
Start with the whole when subtracting. Swapping subtraction numbers changes the answer.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Which subtraction fact belongs with 2 + 5 = 7?
questions.explanation: The whole is 7. Taking away 2 leaves 5.
questions.hint: Use the same three numbers. Start a subtraction fact with the whole, then take away one part.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Which subtraction fact belongs with 3 + 6 = 9?
questions.explanation: The whole is 9. Taking away 3 leaves 6.
questions.hint: Use the same three numbers. Start a subtraction fact with the whole, then take away one part.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Which subtraction fact belongs with 4 + 7 = 11?
questions.explanation: The whole is 11. Taking away 4 leaves 7.
questions.hint: Use the same three numbers. Start a subtraction fact with the whole, then take away one part.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Which subtraction fact belongs with 5 + 8 = 13?
questions.explanation: The whole is 13. Taking away 5 leaves 8.
questions.hint: Use the same three numbers. Start a subtraction fact with the whole, then take away one part.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Which subtraction fact belongs with 2 + 7 = 9?
questions.explanation: The whole is 9. Taking away 2 leaves 7.
questions.hint: Use the same three numbers. Start a subtraction fact with the whole, then take away one part.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Which subtraction fact belongs with 3 + 8 = 11?
questions.explanation: The whole is 11. Taking away 3 leaves 8.
questions.hint: Use the same three numbers. Start a subtraction fact with the whole, then take away one part.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Which subtraction fact belongs with 4 + 9 = 13?
questions.explanation: The whole is 13. Taking away 4 leaves 9.
questions.hint: Use the same three numbers. Start a subtraction fact with the whole, then take away one part.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Which subtraction fact belongs with 6 + 7 = 13?
questions.explanation: The whole is 13. Taking away 6 leaves 7.
questions.hint: Use the same three numbers. Start a subtraction fact with the whole, then take away one part.

lessons.title: Subjects and predicates
lessons.subject: Reading / ELA
notes: The subject tells who or what the sentence is about. The predicate tells what the subject does or is.
In “The kitten sleeps,” “The kitten” is the subject and “sleeps” is the predicate.
Choose a subject that makes sense with the action.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: What is the subject in “The rabbit hops”?
questions.explanation: The rabbit tells who or what the sentence is about.
questions.hint: Find the action first. Ask who or what is doing it. Keep the words that name that person or thing together.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: What is the subject in “My friend reads”?
questions.explanation: My friend tells who or what the sentence is about.
questions.hint: Find the action first. Ask who or what is doing it. Keep the words that name that person or thing together.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: What is the subject in “The puppy runs”?
questions.explanation: The puppy tells who or what the sentence is about.
questions.hint: Find the action first. Ask who or what is doing it. Keep the words that name that person or thing together.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: What is the subject in “Our teacher smiles”?
questions.explanation: Our teacher tells who or what the sentence is about.
questions.hint: Find the action first. Ask who or what is doing it. Keep the words that name that person or thing together.

lessons.title: Writing clear sentences
lessons.subject: Reading / ELA
notes: Begin each sentence with a capital letter and end with punctuation.
Read your sentence aloud to check that it makes sense.
Check spelling and spaces between words.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which sentence begins and ends correctly?
questions.explanation: A sentence starts with a capital and needs end punctuation.
questions.hint: Check the first letter and the ending mark. A telling sentence needs a capital and a period.

lessons.title: Daily review • Day 26
lessons.subject: Math
notes: 35 is 3 tens and 5 ones, or 30 + 5.
Half of 4 is 2: each of two equal groups has 2.
Read the key before counting symbols in a picture graph.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Share 8 counters equally into 2 groups. How many in each group?
questions.explanation: 4 + 4 = 8, so each equal group has 4.
questions.hint: Each part must be the same size. Share one counter at a time between the groups and check they match.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: What is 35 in expanded form?
questions.explanation: 3 tens are 30. Add 5 ones.
questions.hint: Read the tens place, then the ones place. A group of ten is worth more than one single counter.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: A chart shows Ava: ★★★, Ben: ★★★★★. Each star means 1 book. Who read 2 more books?
questions.explanation: Ben read 5 and Ava read 3. 5 − 3 = 2.
questions.hint: Read the chart key. Count each group, then compare the groups named in the question.

lessons.title: Daily review • Day 24
lessons.subject: Reading / ELA
notes: The prefix pre- means before: premix means mix beforehand.
Add apostrophe-s to show ownership: Beth’s flag.
10 more than 7 is 17. Two groups of 3 make 6. A penny is worth one cent.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: What does preheat mean?
questions.explanation: The prefix pre- means before.
questions.hint: Read the base word first. Does the prefix change when the action happens?

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which phrase shows that a flag belongs to Beth?
questions.explanation: Apostrophe-s shows that Beth owns the flag.
questions.hint: Find the owner. Look for the mark that shows something belongs to that person.

lessons.title: Math maintenance
lessons.subject: Math
notes: For two-digit arithmetic, line up tens and ones.
“How many more?” asks for the difference: 16 − 13 = 3.
If some cars plus 3 makes 9, subtract 3 from 9 to find the starting amount: 6.
Compare tens first, then ones. Ordinal numbers tell position: first, second, third, fourth.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: What is 24 + 13?
questions.explanation: Add the tens and the ones: 24 + 13 = 37.
questions.hint: Add tens to tens and ones to ones. Trade ten ones for a ten when needed; check the total.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: What is 24 − 13?
questions.explanation: Take away 13 from 24. Check: 11 + 13 = 24.
questions.hint: Subtract tens and ones. Trade a ten for ten ones when needed, then check by adding back.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: What is 32 + 16?
questions.explanation: Add the tens and the ones: 32 + 16 = 48.
questions.hint: Add tens to tens and ones to ones. Trade ten ones for a ten when needed; check the total.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: What is 32 − 16?
questions.explanation: Take away 16 from 32. Check: 16 + 16 = 32.
questions.hint: Subtract tens and ones. Trade a ten for ten ones when needed, then check by adding back.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: What is 41 + 18?
questions.explanation: Add the tens and the ones: 41 + 18 = 59.
questions.hint: Add tens to tens and ones to ones. Trade ten ones for a ten when needed; check the total.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: What is 41 − 18?
questions.explanation: Take away 18 from 41. Check: 23 + 18 = 41.
questions.hint: Subtract tens and ones. Trade a ten for ten ones when needed, then check by adding back.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: What is 53 + 24?
questions.explanation: Add the tens and the ones: 53 + 24 = 77.
questions.hint: Add tens to tens and ones to ones. Trade ten ones for a ten when needed; check the total.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: What is 53 − 24?
questions.explanation: Take away 24 from 53. Check: 29 + 24 = 53.
questions.hint: Subtract tens and ones. Trade a ten for ten ones when needed, then check by adding back.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: What is 62 + 15?
questions.explanation: Add the tens and the ones: 62 + 15 = 77.
questions.hint: Add tens to tens and ones to ones. Trade ten ones for a ten when needed; check the total.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: What is 62 − 15?
questions.explanation: Take away 15 from 62. Check: 47 + 15 = 62.
questions.hint: Subtract tens and ones. Trade a ten for ten ones when needed, then check by adding back.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: What is 25 + 24?
questions.explanation: Add the tens and the ones: 25 + 24 = 49.
questions.hint: Add tens to tens and ones to ones. Trade ten ones for a ten when needed; check the total.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: What is 25 − 24?
questions.explanation: Take away 24 from 25. Check: 1 + 24 = 25.
questions.hint: Subtract tens and ones. Trade a ten for ten ones when needed, then check by adding back.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Some shells plus 4 makes 11 shells. How many were there at first?
questions.hint: Draw the total and circle the part you know. Count the part still needed to reach the total.

lessons.title: Understanding feelings
lessons.subject: Reading / ELA
notes: Afraid means feeling fear.
Use the words and pictures in a passage to understand how a character feels.
People may feel differently about the same thing; personal reflection has no single correct answer.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: A character is afraid. How does the character feel?
questions.explanation: Afraid means feeling fear.
questions.hint: Put each meaning into the sentence. Which one keeps the idea the same?

lessons.title: Daily review • Day 23
lessons.subject: Math
notes: To subtract 2 on a number line, move two steps left.
A triangle has three straight sides.
If you need 6 stamps and have 4, you need 2 more: 6 − 4 = 2.
Apostrophe-s shows ownership: Chet’s dog.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Which shape has exactly three straight sides?
questions.explanation: A triangle has three straight sides.
questions.hint: Trace each edge with a finger. Count only the straight sides, then compare the choices.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Start at 10 on a number line. Move 2 steps left. Where do you land?
questions.explanation: 10 − 2 = 8. Each left step subtracts 1.
questions.hint: Start at the given number. Each move left takes away one. Count the moves, not the starting spot.

lessons.title: Daily review • Day 21
lessons.subject: Math
notes: Halves are two equal parts of a whole.
28 is 20 + 8, or 2 tens and 8 ones.
Read the labels and key on a picture graph before comparing groups.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Which describes halves?
questions.explanation: Both parts must be equal to be halves.
questions.hint: Check both how many parts there are and whether the parts are the same size.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: How many tens and ones make 28?
questions.explanation: 2 tens are 20, and 20 + 8 = 28.
questions.hint: Read the tens place, then the ones place. A group of ten is worth more than one single counter.

lessons.title: At the Library • comprehension
lessons.subject: Reading / ELA
notes: The narrator can walk or ride a bike to the neighborhood library.
Choosing among many books is difficult. The narrator selects fiction and nonfiction.
After choosing books, the narrator enjoys games in the computer room.
Find details in the passage to support your answer. Fiction tells imagined stories; nonfiction gives factual information.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: In At the Library, how does the narrator get to the library?
questions.explanation: The passage says the library is in the neighborhood, so walking or biking is possible.
questions.hint: Find the sentence in the story that explains the trip. Choose only what that sentence supports.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: In At the Library, what happens after choosing books?
questions.explanation: The narrator chooses books before using the computer room.
questions.hint: Reread that part of the story. Find the named event, then look at what the narrator does next.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which kind of book gives factual information?
questions.explanation: Nonfiction gives factual information about real subjects.
questions.hint: Decide whether the book explains real information or tells an imagined story.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 • Jesus Is God’s Best Gift
lessons.subject: Religion
notes: God the Father sent Jesus, his Son, to save us. Jesus teaches us about the Father and how to live.
Grace is the new life Jesus gives us. Jesus died and rose from the dead. He is our Savior.
A disciple knows, loves, and follows Jesus. Baptism makes us members of his Church. The Holy Spirit guides the Church.
Jesus compares himself to a vine and us to its branches. Our good deeds are its fruit.
The Sign of the Cross remembers Jesus’ love and that he saved us. Pray: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: What is the name for the new life Jesus gives us?
questions.explanation: The Chapter 2 page calls Jesus’ gift of new life grace.
questions.hint: Think about sharing in God’s life. Which lesson word names that special gift of life?
questions.sourceFact: Chapter 2 • Jesus Is God’s Best Gift

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: Who guides the Church?
questions.explanation: The Holy Spirit helps the Church live and love like Jesus.
questions.hint: Remember the helper Jesus promised to his followers. Think about who continues to guide the Church.
questions.sourceFact: Chapter 2 • Jesus Is God’s Best Gift

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: What does a disciple do?
choices: Learns about Jesus but ignores his teaching
Follows Jesus only when it is easy
Asks for help but never helps others
questions.explanation: A disciple lives according to Jesus’ teaching.
questions.hint: Think about what a follower does, not just what that person knows.
questions.sourceFact: Chapter 2 • Jesus Is God’s Best Gift

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: In the vine and branches comparison, who is the vine?
questions.explanation: Jesus is the vine; we are the branches.
questions.hint: In the comparison, the vine gives life to its branches. Who gives life to the followers?
questions.sourceFact: Chapter 2 • Jesus Is God’s Best Gift

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: What do the fruits represent in that comparison?
questions.explanation: Good deeds are ways to live closer to Jesus.
questions.hint: A fruit shows what a plant produces. Think of the loving actions a follower can produce.
questions.sourceFact: Chapter 2 • Jesus Is God’s Best Gift

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: Which sacrament makes us members of the Church?
questions.explanation: Through Baptism we share in Jesus’ life and belong to his Church.
questions.hint: Think of the sacrament at the beginning of life in the Church, when water is used.
questions.sourceFact: Chapter 2 • Jesus Is God’s Best Gift

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: What do we remember when praying the Sign of the Cross?
questions.answer: Jesus’ love and that he saved us
choices: That prayer replaces every kind act
Jesus’ love and that he saved us
That God cares only on special days
questions.explanation: The cross reminds us of Jesus’ love and saving action.
questions.hint: Think about the shape traced in the prayer and what Jesus did out of love.
questions.sourceFact: Chapter 2 • Jesus Is God’s Best Gift

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: Who sent Jesus to save us?
questions.explanation: God the Father sent his Son, Jesus.
questions.hint: Think about the relationship between Jesus and the one who sent him.
questions.sourceFact: Chapter 2 • Jesus Is God’s Best Gift

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: What happened after Jesus died?
choices: His followers forgot all his teachings
He stopped caring about his followers
questions.explanation: Jesus died and rose from the dead. He is our Savior.
questions.hint: Recall the Easter part of the lesson. Death was not the end of the story.
questions.sourceFact: Chapter 2 • Jesus Is God’s Best Gift

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: Which action is a good way to follow Jesus?
choices: Ignore a classmate who is left out
Refuse to share when someone needs help
Only help when a prize is promised
questions.explanation: Kindness and helping others are good deeds.
questions.hint: Choose an action that shows care for another person, not just a wish to be noticed.
questions.sourceFact: Chapter 2 • Jesus Is God’s Best Gift

lessons.title: Daily review • Day 22
lessons.subject: Reading / ELA
notes: Snug means cozy and warm.
Alphabetical order: black, plus, sled.
23 can be written as 2 tens and 3 ones, or 23 ones.
In a part-whole model, the parts add to the whole.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which word comes first in ABC order: sled, black, plus?
questions.explanation: Compare first letters: b comes before p and s.
questions.hint: Compare the first letters using the alphabet. If they match, move to the next letter.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which phrase means the bed belongs to Jen?
questions.explanation: Apostrophe-s after Jen shows ownership.
questions.hint: Find the owner. Look for the mark that shows something belongs to that person.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: An hour has how many minutes?
questions.explanation: There are 60 minutes in an hour.
questions.hint: Picture the minute hand making one full turn. Count the minutes around the clock.

lessons.title: Theme and supporting details
lessons.subject: Reading / ELA
notes: A theme is the message or lesson a story communicates; it is broader than one event.
Supporting details are specific character actions or events that show why a theme fits.
Use several details from the story to support a theme instead of relying on one isolated detail.
The uploaded organizer practices identifying a theme and connecting four details to it; the child’s written responses are not treated as an answer key.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which choice is a theme rather than a single story detail?
questions.explanation: A theme is a message that can apply beyond one moment in the story.
questions.hint: Ask which choice sounds like a lesson or message, not one event.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which detail best supports the theme “Friends help one another”?
questions.answer: A friend stops to help carry a heavy box.
choices: A friend stops to help carry a heavy box.
The friends walk past a tree.
questions.explanation: Helping with a problem is evidence for a theme about friends helping.
questions.hint: Choose the event that actually shows someone helping.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Why is it better to use several details when explaining a story’s theme?
questions.answer: Several details show that the message appears across the story.
choices: Several details show that the message appears across the story.
One detail always proves every possible theme.
Details are only used to tell where the story happens.
A theme must be the longest sentence in the story.
questions.explanation: Repeated evidence makes the theme explanation stronger and more accurate.
questions.hint: Look for a pattern across the story, not just one moment.

lessons.title: My Baptism Story • Trimester 1 project
lessons.subject: Religion
notes: Complete the Baptism story worksheet using accurate family information rather than guessing personal details.
The worksheet asks about the Baptism date, age, priest, church, whether the child cried, godparents, why the godparents were chosen, clothing, and how the family celebrated.
The colored project page must include at least one Baptism picture.
The rubric gives 5 points each for completion, neatness, pictures, and presentation.
The visible due-date line reads “Friday Oct. 21.” Because October 21, 2026 is a Wednesday, this date is held as unconfirmed and is not promoted to the app calendar without another source.

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: What must be included on the colored paper for the Baptism project?
questions.answer: At least one picture from the Baptism.
choices: At least one picture from the Baptism.
A copy of a report card.
questions.explanation: The project directions require at least one Baptism picture.
questions.hint: Check the project directions for the picture requirement.

questions.subject: Religion
questions.prompt: Which item is one of the project rubric categories?
questions.explanation: The rubric lists completion, neatness, pictures, and presentation.
questions.hint: Look at the four rubric lines on the project sheet.

lessons.title: Daily review • Day 25 • Reading / ELA
lessons.subject: Reading / ELA
notes: Apostrophe-s can show ownership: a friend’s pet.
A common noun names a person, place, animal, or thing.
On this review, slob means a very messy person, dim means not very bright or clear, and kin means people in your family.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly shows that the toy belongs to Mia?
questions.explanation: Apostrophe-s after Mia shows ownership.
questions.hint: Add apostrophe-s to the owner’s name.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: What kind of noun is “cat” in the sentence “Can a cat swim?”
questions.explanation: A cat is an animal.
questions.hint: Classify what the noun names.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which word means “people in your family”?
questions.explanation: Kin means relatives or family members.
questions.hint: Think about relatives.

lessons.title: Daily review • Day 25 • Math
lessons.subject: Math
notes: Use basic addition and subtraction facts within 10 accurately.
20 is 2 tens and 0 ones.
When a problem gives a total and one part, subtract to find the part that is left.
Use shorter and longer to compare object lengths.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: What is 9 − 3?
questions.explanation: Taking 3 away from 9 leaves 6.
questions.hint: Count back three from 9.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: How many tens and ones are in 20?
questions.explanation: Twenty is two groups of ten with no ones left over.
questions.hint: Split 20 into groups of ten.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: There are 9 pets. Three are dogs and the rest are fish. How many are fish?
questions.explanation: Subtract the 3 dogs from the 9 total pets: 9 − 3 = 6.
questions.hint: The total is 9 and one part is 3.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: A ribbon is 8 inches long and another ribbon is 5 inches long. Which word describes the 5-inch ribbon?
questions.explanation: Five inches is less length than eight inches, so it is shorter.
questions.hint: Compare the two lengths.

lessons.title: Daily review • Day 27 • Reading / ELA
lessons.subject: Reading / ELA
notes: Proper nouns name specific people, places, brands, or titles and begin with capital letters.
The spelling review sorts words by beginning blends such as dr- and tr-.
Knack means a special skill or something a person is good at.
Antonyms are words with opposite meanings.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which word should begin with a capital letter because it is a specific place name?
questions.explanation: Amazon is a specific name, so it is a proper noun.
questions.hint: Specific names are capitalized.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which word begins with the dr- blend?
questions.explanation: Drill begins with d and r together.
questions.hint: Say the first two sounds slowly.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: If Maya has a knack for drawing, what does that mean?
questions.answer: She is especially good at drawing.
choices: She is especially good at drawing.
questions.explanation: A knack is a natural or practiced skill.
questions.hint: Replace knack with “special skill.”

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which word is an antonym of “cold”?
questions.explanation: Warm has the opposite meaning of cold.
questions.hint: An antonym means opposite.

lessons.title: Daily review • Day 27 • Math
lessons.subject: Math
notes: Pairs such as 2 and 3 or 0 and 5 can make 5.
30 is 3 tens and 0 ones.
To tell time to the hour, read the number the short hour hand points to when the minute hand is at 12.
When objects leave a group, subtract to find how many remain.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Which pair makes 5?
questions.explanation: Two plus three equals five.
questions.hint: Add the two numbers in each pair.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: How can 30 be written in tens and ones?
questions.explanation: Three tens equals thirty.
questions.hint: Count groups of ten.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: When the minute hand points to 12 and the hour hand points to 10, what time is it?
questions.explanation: At an exact hour the minute hand is on 12, and the hour hand names the hour.
questions.hint: Read the short hand for the hour.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Eight jets are on the ground. Four fly away. How many are left?
questions.explanation: Eight minus four equals four.
questions.hint: Take away the four that left.

lessons.title: Daily review • Day 28 • Reading / ELA
lessons.subject: Reading / ELA
notes: Capitalize specific names such as a store, person, state, or place.
A proper noun is the exact name of a person, place, or thing.
Knack means a special ability or something a person is especially good at.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses capitalization correctly?
questions.answer: We bought a backpack at Walmart.
choices: We bought a backpack at Walmart.
We bought a backpack at walmart.
we bought a backpack at Walmart.
We Bought A Backpack At Walmart.
questions.explanation: Walmart is a specific name and the sentence begins with a capital letter.
questions.hint: Capitalize the first word and specific names.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which word is a proper noun?
questions.explanation: Hawaii is the specific name of a place.
questions.hint: Ask which word names one exact place.

questions.subject: Reading / ELA
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses “knack” correctly?
questions.answer: My teacher has a knack for explaining hard ideas clearly.
choices: My teacher has a knack for explaining hard ideas clearly.
The knack barked at the mail carrier.
I put my lunch inside a knack.
We measured the knack with a ruler.
questions.explanation: Knack means a special skill or ability.
questions.hint: Try replacing knack with “special skill.”

lessons.title: Daily review • Day 28 • Math
lessons.subject: Math
notes: To add 2 on a number line, move two spaces to the right.
Thirty-four is 34 and thirty-nine is 39.
A pentagon has 5 straight sides.
“How many fewer?” asks for the difference between two amounts.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Start at 6 on a number line and add 2. Where do you land?
questions.explanation: Move two spaces right from 6: 7, then 8.
questions.hint: Adding moves right on the number line.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: Which numeral matches “thirty-nine”?
questions.explanation: Thirty-nine has 3 tens and 9 ones.
questions.hint: Listen for thirty = 3 tens and nine = 9 ones.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: How many straight sides does a pentagon have?
questions.explanation: A pentagon is a five-sided polygon.
questions.hint: The prefix penta- points to five.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: There are 9 red vans and 5 black vans. How many fewer black vans are there?
questions.explanation: Find the difference: 9 − 5 = 4.
questions.hint: “How many fewer” means compare by subtraction.
